title: Affine-lift descent respects cover refinements and smooth pullback
statement:
Use fine monoschemes, fans, coherent monoid ideals, saturated blowup towers, recursive pullback, and contraction as in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $\mathscr C$ be the full category of fine monoschemes with finite affine covers such that both their ordinary stalk group completions and the group completions of their sharpened stalks are torsion free. Let $R$ be a smooth-functorial saturated desingularization rule on $\mathscr C$, with centers and order retained and with identity and composition compatibility. For a fine torsion-free fan $F$ with finite affine cover $\mathcal U=\{U_i\simeq S(P_i)\}$ by sharp fine monoids, let $T_{\mathcal U}$ be the tower obtained by gluing the sharpened uncontracted component restrictions of the single tower $R(\coprod_i\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}P_i)$, using the identity comparisons of the overlap ideals and fraction charts. These glued towers exist as in [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent].

For any two such covers $\mathcal U,\mathcal V$, the restriction of the single tower on the disjoint union of the lifts for $\mathcal U\amalg\mathcal V$ to either subunion, followed by contraction, is the assigned tower there. A stage of this combined tower is removable on every member of $\mathcal U$ if and only if it is removable on every member of $\mathcal V$. Thus the two restrictions delete the same original indices, and $T_{\mathcal U}$ and $T_{\mathcal V}$ are canonically identified with the same centers, order and arrows. These comparisons are compatible with further cover refinements. The same identification holds when any of the sharp affine lifts is replaced by another affine lift in $\mathscr C$ over that affine fan. Denote the cover-independent tower by $T_R(F)$.

For every smooth fan morphism $g:G\to F$ between fine torsion-free fans with finite affine covers there is a canonical identification
$$T_R(G)\simeq(g^*T_R(F))^c.$$
On the smallest neighborhoods of a point and its image, the map on sharp monoids is $B\to B\oplus\mathbf N^r$ and is induced by the corresponding smooth map of sharp affine monoscheme models. After localization at any point, the local monoid map of this unsharpened affine monoscheme morphism has form $B'\to B'\oplus\mathbf N^{r-t}\oplus\mathbf Z^t$. In a single disjoint union containing the finitely many source and target affine models, the local comparison identifies every pulled-back ideal and fraction chart at its inherited uncontracted index. A global index is deleted exactly when its pulled-back center is the whole sheaf and its arrow is an isomorphism, equivalently when both conditions hold locally everywhere. The comparisons respect identities and composition, on indices and on every level map. In particular for composable smooth maps $H\xrightarrow hG\xrightarrow gF$ the surviving subsequence and level maps obtained by successive contractions agree with those obtained by contracting $(gh)^*T_R(F)$ once; before contraction the ideals satisfy $(gh)^*I=h^*(g^*I)$ and the fraction maps are the corresponding substitutions. Deleting a whole-ideal isomorphism leaves every later ideal and its pullbacks unchanged under the canonical identification of its source and target.

source.place: ILO VIII 3.1.13--3.1.16, 3.1.22, 3.1.25--3.1.27, pp.100--102, and Remark 2.3.5(ii)--(iii), p.92; refinement, local smooth pullback and contraction coherence (returned proof steps 11--13). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text: Put $L_{\mathcal U}=\coprod_i\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P_i$ and similarly $L_{\mathcal V}$, and apply $R$ once to $D=L_{\mathcal U}\amalg L_{\mathcal V}$. These objects lie in $\mathscr C$ by [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent]. The component inclusions are smooth, since their stalk maps are identities. The assumed functoriality of $R$ identifies the contraction of $R(D)|_{L_{\mathcal U}}$ with $R(L_{\mathcal U})$, including centers and arrows; likewise for $\mathcal V$. By [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison] and [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization], sharpening retains exactly these original indices and these contraction tests. Apply [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent] to the combined cover: its full component restrictions glue to a single tower $W$ on $F$. Thus the restrictions to either subcover are restrictions of this same $W$ before any contraction.

source.place: VIII 3.1.25--3.1.27, p.102; Remark 2.3.5(ii), p.92; combined-cover construction.

proof.text: At a fixed original index of $W$, its ideal $J$ is the whole sheaf if and only if $0$ belongs to $J$ locally at every point: representatives of these germs cover the space, and the subsheaf gluing condition gives $0\in J$ on every open. Its arrow is an isomorphism if and only if its restrictions over a covering are isomorphisms: the local inverses agree on overlaps, since each is inverse to the same arrow, and their maps and section homomorphisms glue to an inverse. Apply these tests at each level, covered by the inverse images of either $\mathcal U$ or $\mathcal V$. A stage is removable on every member of one cover exactly when it is removable on every member of the other. Delete that common subsequence, in its inherited order. Step 1 and the uniqueness of the glued tower in [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent] identify the results with $T_{\mathcal U}$ and $T_{\mathcal V}$. In fact $W$ is globally contracted by that same lemma, so no original stage can disappear on an entire subcover of $F$. A stage removable on only some charts is still retained.

source.place: VIII 3.1.22, 3.1.26--3.1.27, pp.101--102; Remark 2.3.5(ii), p.92; explicit locality and deletion test.

proof.text: For three covers, use the rule on the disjoint union of all their lifts. The two-cover argument identifies every comparison with restriction of its identical local center ideals, followed by deletion of the same globally removable original indices. On an $a$-chart of a center $I$, the comparison fixes each element of $P$ and each difference $b-a$, and therefore fixes the generated monoid $P[I-a]$, its saturation, and every localization used for a chart overlap. This is precisely the fraction comparison specified by [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison]. Consequently the direct comparison and either composite agree on every chart and every level. The same construction includes any further finite refinement, and proves the cover-comparison cocycle without choosing an affine intersection. Write $T_R(F)$ for the tower so identified.

source.place: VIII 3.1.25--3.1.27, p.102; Remark 2.3.5(ii)--(iii), p.92; refinement cocycle on centers and fraction charts.

proof.text: Consider another affine lift $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P\in\mathscr C$ whose sharpening is the given affine fan $S(B)$. By [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections], global sharp sections identify $P/P^\times$ with $B$. Both $P^{\rm gp}$ and $B^{\rm gp}$ are torsion free: these are the ordinary and sharp stalks at the unique closed point. Thus [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-splitting] gives $P\simeq B\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ over $B$. For two lifts use $B\oplus\mathbf Z^{s+t}$, mapping to each by adjoining the other free group. These maps are smooth and surjective: ideals are invariant under translation by units, so primes of each product with a group are exactly inverse images of primes of $B$. The common model lies in $\mathscr C$, since its group completion is torsion free and its sharp stalks are those of $S(B)$. Put both lifts into one disjoint union. The two-smooth-maps assertion of [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization] identifies their full pulled-back towers on this common model. Sharpening, by [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison], identifies the ideals and fraction charts over the identity of $S(B)$, independently of the splittings. Steps 2--3 give exactly the same contracted global tower and comparisons after any finite lift replacements.

source.place: VIII 3.1.11, 3.1.13, 3.1.25--3.1.27, pp.100--102; Remark 2.3.5(iii), p.92; comparison of arbitrary affine lifts.

proof.text: Fix a smooth $g:G\to F$ and $y\in G$, with $x=g(y)$. By [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent], the smallest neighborhoods $G_y,F_x$ are affine. They have sharp section monoids equal to their stalks, by [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections]. Continuity sends generalizations of $y$ to generalizations of $x$, so $g$ restricts to $G_y\to F_x$. Put $B=\mathcal P_{F,x}$. Smoothness says the stalk map is $B\to B\oplus\mathbf N^r$. The natural Hom/sections bijection of [lem-trf-affine-fan-hom-universal] says the entire restricted fan map is induced by this homomorphism. Its sharp affine monoscheme models belong to $\mathscr C$ by [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent], applied to these open fans. Only finitely many such models are needed: a prime in a monoid generated by $k$ elements is determined by which generators lie in its complementary face, giving at most $2^k$ primes. The face is generated by precisely these generators, as follows by expanding a sum and using primality. Each finite affine cover therefore has a finite underlying space; use all its point neighborhoods.

source.place: VIII 3.1.8(ii), 3.1.10(ii), 3.1.13--3.1.16, pp.99--100; explicit local fan models and finiteness.

proof.text:
The monoscheme map induced by $B\to B\oplus\mathbf N^r$ is smooth at every point, not just at its closed point. Indeed take a prime of $B\oplus\mathbf N^r$ and its image in $B$. If a sum is in its complementary face, each summand is in that face. The face is therefore the sum of a face of $B$ and the submonoid generated by a subset of the free coordinates. Localizing gives
$$B'\longrightarrow B'\oplus\mathbf N^{r-t}\oplus\mathbf Z^t,$$
where $B'$ is the localization of $B$ at the image prime and $t$ is the number of inverted free coordinates. This is exactly the defining smooth form. More generally, localizing such a product at any further point repeats the same computation. All induced morphisms to component opens of a disjoint union are smooth as well, because open inclusions do not alter stalks.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.1.14 and 3.1.15--3.1.16, p.100; explicit localization calculation.

proof.text: Choose the point-neighborhood covers of $F$ and $G$ from Step 5, and let $D$ now be the single disjoint union of all their sharp affine monoscheme models. Write $Q=R(D)$ with its original index set. At $y$, the source model has two smooth maps to $D$: its own component inclusion, and its smooth map to the target model followed by that component inclusion. By [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization] these two maps pull back $Q$ to canonically identical full towers, with all original centers. No surjectivity onto $D$ is required for this assertion. By [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison], their sharpenings identify the source tower with the recursively pulled-back target tower at each inherited index; the chart map sends a difference $b-a$ to $g(b)-g(a)$. On overlapping source neighborhoods these are the same pulled-back ideal subsheaves and the same substitutions in fractions, so the comparisons agree there. Induction on the index, starting with $G\to F$, applies this argument to the next identified ideal and its saturated fraction charts. Using the gluing assertion of [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent], the raw source restriction tower is thus the recursive pullback of the raw target restriction tower, at all original indices.

source.place: VIII 3.1.22--3.1.27, pp.101--102; Remark 2.3.5(iii), p.92; one disjoint union synchronizes all smooth local comparisons.

proof.text:
We may contract these raw comparisons compatibly. In a local smooth product chart, [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization] gives level monoids $P_i\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$, and saturation of this monoid is equivalent to saturation of $P_i$. Thus a whole-ideal isomorphism stage remains one under smooth recursive pullback: its pulled-back ideal is still whole, and its source is saturated whenever the target of this unit-ideal saturated blowup is saturated. The blowup of the whole ideal has chart $P_i$ before saturation by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Deleting such a stage replaces an isomorphism by its inverse identification, so every subsequent ideal and fraction substitution is the same after transport. This also proves, by induction through the finite original index list, that deletion followed by further smooth pullback and contraction equals smooth pullback followed by contraction once. The contracted source restriction of $Q$ is its assigned $R$ on the source subunion, by functoriality for that open inclusion, and likewise for the target subunion. Sharpening preserves exactly the contraction tests by [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization]. Step 7 followed by the local tests of Step 2 therefore gives
$$T_R(G)\simeq(g^*T_R(F))^c.$$
At a retained index the center is the generated image of the target center, and the arrow is its saturated blowup. The chart comparisons above fix the order and every level map.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, 3.1.22, 3.1.25--3.1.27, pp.101--102; contraction under smooth pullback and assembly of the comparison.

proof.text:
For composition $H\xrightarrow hG\xrightarrow gF$, let $I$ be a center at an original index. Locally $g^*I$ consists of sums $g(a)+q$ with $a\in I$ and $q$ a source monoid section. Its further generated image consists of sums $h(g(a))+h(q)+u$. This equals the ideal generated by the $h(g(a))$: one inclusion uses closure under addition, the other takes $q=0$. Hence $h^*(g^*I)=(gh)^*I$. The chart substitutions compose too:
$$b-a\longmapsto g(b)-g(a)\longmapsto h(g(b))-h(g(a)).$$
They agree on the original monoid and its adjoined fractions, hence on its saturation inside the group completion and on localized overlaps. Induct on the original index, using equality of the current ideals to identify the next saturated charts. This yields identical full recursive towers and level maps before contraction. The fraction substitutions used here are exactly those specified by [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison].

source.place: VIII 3.1.22, 3.1.25--3.1.27, pp.101--102; generated-image ideals and explicit fraction substitutions for composition.

proof.text: Each index removed after pullback along $g$ remains removable after the further smooth pullback along $h$, by Step 8. At every other index Step 9 identifies the tests on the final pullbacks: the ideal is whole and the same arrow is an isomorphism in either construction. Transport over an already deleted whole-ideal isomorphism leaves the next ideal unchanged, as shown in Step 8. Induction along the ordered original indices therefore gives precisely the same surviving subsequence for successive contractions as for contracting $(gh)^*T_R(F)$ once. The level maps agree by the substitutions of Step 9 and the inverse identifications at deleted stages. For an identity morphism those substitutions are identities and the globally contracted tower loses no index. The local comparisons agree on every overlap by Step 7; gluing the identical local maps gives identical global maps. Step 3 makes these statements independent of the covers used for $F,G,H$, and Step 4 makes them independent of the affine lifts. This proves both identity and composition compatibility, including all indices and level maps.

source.place: VIII 3.1.22, 3.1.25--3.1.27, pp.101--102; Remark 2.3.5(ii)--(iii), p.92; comparison coherence after contraction.

proof.text: The empty fan is included: [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent] gives its length-zero tower. Pullback to the empty fan has whole ideals and empty isomorphism arrows at every original stage, so contraction deletes every index. A map from a nonempty fan to the empty fan does not exist. The same proof also permits length zero on a nonempty fan, free rank $r=0$, and a cover with repeated members: the index tests and the displayed identities then have the indicated vacuous or identity meanings. A nonidentity initial saturation with whole ideal is retained throughout, since every deletion above requires both the whole-ideal condition and an isomorphism arrow.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, 3.1.22, 3.1.26--3.1.27, pp.101--102; empty and initial-saturation cases.

proof_origin.place: Expanded proof of ILO VIII 3.1.26--3.1.27 using 3.1.8(ii), 3.1.13--3.1.16, 3.1.22, 3.1.25 and Remark 2.3.5(ii)--(iii); explicit cover-index, localized smoothness and contraction-coherence arguments.
